evidenceDecision: Real HTTP tests exercise authentication, PIN/rate budgets, cookies and browser admission; real request/response semantics are the security boundary. v0.8.5: Configured passwords accept 8–1024 Unicode characters with a recommendation warning below 15. Direct boundary tests cover ASCII/Unicode and CLI/environment ingestion; session, Origin and throttling evidence remains mandatory. Agent CLI (FM-WORLDCLI): the `/api/world/cli` bearer path is tested directly for loopback-only, no-Origin admission, a derived CLI token that the login credential cannot replace, wrong and missing tokens, and a throttle that never blocks the owner's login. Pane attribution is a pure check of the caller's process ancestry against Herdr's pane process info, tested with spoofed panes, a second connection on the same port from another loopback address, ambiguous rows, shared sockets, IPv6, unknown processes and remote hosts. End to end in a throwaway Herdr session, an in-pane call was verified and the same pane ID from another process was not; the port-collision case is covered only by the synthetic /proc tests. No ordering or recovery protocol is added, so a model would restate these checks. Owner ask withdrawal (#472) compares the verified original connection, runtime, terminal and agent-session digest. Service regressions cover cause-key deduplication, foreign/unverified refusal, idempotent withdrawal, answer preservation and rejection of later answers; the existing endpoint/process ownership fixtures remain mandatory. Per-World cookie (#1250): the session cookie is named by a digest of the World's signing secret; direct tests cover two Worlds with different secrets sharing one host's cookie jar (unit and real HTTP), two Worlds swapping ports, a session moving once from the legacy shared name without changing its token, logout clearing every cookie a later request is accepted with after visits through 40 ports, a World staying logged in while 24 previews log in after it, pruning expired World cookies and live ones beyond 48 least recently set first, the unsigned hour stamp never validating a forged token, and return paths refusing other origins, `//`, backslashes, control characters, dot-segment normalisation to `//` and `token`. No ordering or recovery state is added: admission is a pure function of the request's cookies. CLI caller verification (#1492): bounded macOS lsof/ps fixtures cover IPv4/mapped/IPv6 endpoints, reversed endpoints, wrong ports/addresses, shared owners, ambiguous sockets, numeric ancestry, cycles and all inspection limits. An injected linux/darwin/win32 × TUI/core × matching/foreign/unknown ancestry matrix exercises the shared identity resolver. CLI tests enumerate refusal codes and true/false/null/absent recording receipts, preserve exit 3 without fallback on refusal, and exercise actual dropped and malformed HTTP replies as unknown. These are bounded observation and synchronous output decisions with no new writer or retry ordering; no additional Quint state machine is warranted. Real macOS tool and runtime verification remains an explicit owner/platform prerequisite, not claimed by fixtures.
